text: Why is the occurrence of smog particularly common in industrial regions?
options: Because industrial regions typically have the cleanest air of any region
Because smog can only ever form directly over the sea
Because industrial regions receive the least rainfall of any region
Because smoke and soot released by industries combine with fog and other pollutants under calm, cool conditions to form smog
explanation: Industrial areas release large quantities of smoke, soot and chemical pollutants; when these combine with naturally occurring fog, especially under calm, cool atmospheric conditions that trap pollutants near the ground, dense smog results.

text: Why is the white marble of the Taj Mahal gradually getting corroded and discoloured over time?
options: Because of unusually heavy rainfall in the region with no connection to pollution
Because of natural ageing of the marble, with pollution playing no role at all
Because of frequent earthquakes in the region
Because acidic pollutants (such as sulphur dioxide from nearby industries and traffic) react with the calcium carbonate in the marble, causing it to erode (a form of acid rain damage)
explanation: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides released by nearby industries and vehicles dissolve in atmospheric moisture to form acidic compounds; these react chemically with the calcium carbonate in marble, gradually corroding and yellowing the Taj Mahal's surface.

text: Why do fossil fuels contribute heavily to air pollution when burned?
options: Because fossil fuels burn completely cleanly, releasing only water vapour
Because burning fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum releases carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide and particulate matter into the atmosphere
Because fossil fuels have no connection to air pollution at all
Because fossil fuels only ever pollute water, never air
explanation: The combustion of coal, petroleum and natural gas releases a range of pollutants, including carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and fine particulate matter, which together degrade air quality and contribute to phenomena such as smog and acid rain.

text: Why are pesticides and fertilizers harmful to aquatic life when they run off into water bodies?
options: Because they evaporate completely before ever reaching any water body
Because they affect only birds, not fish or aquatic plants
Because they always increase the oxygen levels in water to harmful excess
Because runoff carries these chemicals into rivers and lakes, where they can poison aquatic organisms directly or cause excessive algae growth (eutrophication) that depletes the water's oxygen
explanation: Excess pesticides and fertilizers washed off farmland by rain enter rivers and lakes; some chemicals directly poison fish and other aquatic life, while nutrient-rich fertilizer runoff can trigger excessive algal growth that, upon decomposing, depletes dissolved oxygen and suffocates aquatic organisms.

text: Which of the following gases is a major contributor to the formation of acid rain?
options: Oxygen
Argon
Sulphur dioxide
Nitrogen
explanation: Sulphur dioxide (along with nitrogen oxides), released mainly from burning fossil fuels, dissolves in atmospheric moisture to form sulphuric acid, which falls to the ground as acid rain, damaging buildings, soil and water bodies.

text: Why are trees commonly planted in and around factory/industrial areas?
options: Because trees improve the durability of factory machinery
Because they are required purely for the factory's building design and have no environmental purpose
Because trees are grown there only as a fuel source for the factory
Because trees absorb certain air pollutants and release oxygen, helping to filter the air and reduce the impact of industrial pollution
explanation: Trees act as natural air filters, absorbing carbon dioxide and certain pollutants (and some particulate matter settles on leaves) while releasing oxygen through photosynthesis, helping to offset some of the air pollution generated by nearby industrial activity.
